newsitem.title: USA: PepsiCo profits up; details restaurant spin-off.
newsitem.headline: PepsiCo profits up; details restaurant spin-off.

text.p: PepsiCo Inc. Tuesday reported an 8 percent rise in earnings for the first quarter, and detailed its plan to divest its KFC, Taco Bell and Pizza Hut restaurant operations.

Led by strong North American sales of Pepsi and Mountain Dew soft drinks, the Purchase, N.Y.-based company posted profits of $427 million, or 27 cents a share, on sales of $6.7 billion vs. year-earlier profits of $394 million, or 24 cents a share, on sales of $6.55 billion.
The earnings beat Wall Street's estimate of 23 cents a share, and Pepsico's stock jumped $2.875 to $34.125 on the New York Stock Exchange.
Analysts said the first quarter results boosted Wall Street's confidence in the company and its restructuring plan.
"I think this indicates the turn from PepsiCo that investors have been waiting for," said Emanuel Goldman, an analyst for PaineWebber.
Case sales grew 6 percent, driven by double-digit volume growth for Mountain Dew and solid growth in Pepsi, the company said.
Roger Enrico, PepsiCo's chairman, said the company was on track with its strategy of divesting its restaurants so as to focus on beverages and snack foods.
"We refranchised 94 stores this quarter and for the full year expect to sell as many or more than we did last year," Enrico said.
He said the company was readying for a spin-off of its quick service restaurant business including preparing and filing a ruling request with the Internal Revenue Service.
Enrico said PepsiCo had completed the sale of both East Side Mario's and Hot 'n Now and it is in active talks to sell both California Pizza Kitchen and PFS, a restaurant distribution company.
Analysts particularly were pleased with PepsiCo's beverage results in the international arena, where the company hopes to challenge rival Coca-Cola Co.
Although international sales were down 14 percent, and volume fell 3 percent, Pepsi noted that the volume rate of decline had slowed from the 9 percent drop in the fourth quarter of 1996.
"The numbers are excellent," said Martin Romm, an analyst for Credit Suisse First Boston. "This is a very solid performance."
Worldwide restaurant profits rose 7 percent as a result of strong results in the international business and a modest increase in the United States, PepsiCo said.
In its snacks division, Frito Lay sales rose 7 percent and its profit increased 15 percent. Internationally, Frito Lay's sales grew by 13 percent and profits jumped 36 percent.
Pizza Hut, the largest brand, had a drop in same-store sales, or sales from stores open at least a year, of 8 percent.
KFC and Taco Bell posted same-store sales growth of 4 percent in the quarter. In Taco Bell's case, the key driver was the success of a promotion linked to the "Star Wars" film series, PepsiCo said.
